If you review Cookiemonster please write how it behaves compared to TR14.

It felt smoother, almost like NNLC was on, but would still have minor oscillation every now and then. Still has too much right over-steer and not enough left steer for turns/curvs, but felt good in the lane.

TR14 felt too twitchy for me, I like TR13 more. TR13 is also better about the over/under steer issue, if anything it could be tuned just a tiny bit more (still over steers to the right on a right turn, but it’s super minor) and it would be perfect.
I place CTR right in between TR13 and TR14

I liked TR14 a lot more than TR13 on both of my cars. Cookiemonster feels closer to the problems I had with TR13. For my Toyota it failed one big curve that TR7 and TR14 previously handled. It feels mushy on turns. At low speeds it feels like it attempts to steer less than TR14. Feels less "locked in" to lane than TR14.

**Update: I think I know what Cookiemonster is doing. TR14 has a lot more fine-grained steering adjustments while Cookiemonster appears to be attempting larger jerks. Toyota's weak torque limits means those large jerks fail. Then what feels like weak turns is the model giving up.**

Trying this on my hkg-angle next.

I guess its up to personal preference (though, our cars are very likely acting differently with different models). TR14 feels like it is more "locked in", but my steering wheel looks like a metronome. TR13 and definitely DTR3 with NNLC could be seen as slow or mushy, but it never leaves the lane.
To clarify, when I say looks like a metronome, I'm not talking about oscillation, I'm just talking about the act of staying in the lane
CTR moves the steering wheel more slowly, it feels more natural to me
Have you played with software delay yet?
I have, It feels nicer with delay enabled
Oh crap that never got pulled into devc3. No I made it user adjustable late last night lol
Oh, that, no
I will once I get the chance
Weird how adding delay could be helpful, I always figured less delay was better
Well you can reduce delay once these changes hit. The default is 0.2 haha. That was the default before liveDelay was introduced

I think reducing delay helps up to a point. We're trying to figure out what that point is. It could be a floating offset above `lateralDelay` or it could be a software-overhead fixed floor somewhere above `lateralDelay` where it makes the model behave better because it was somehow "too low".
That floor needs to be tested with NNLC enabled and disabled separately. Different code. NNLC does quite a lot with the delay because it also plans ahead by the same duration.

I tried various values above `lateralDelay` today. In my case it made TR14 seemingly behave better. Unclear what is the ideal value. People should experiment with it and independently come up with their own theory.
Worth noting that point is also different on most vehicles as well

NNLC from April to June of this year was adding a fixed +0.3 seconds to `steeringActuatorDelay`. That's `0.1` seconds on HKG or `0.12` seconds on Toyota. The current NNLC is instead using exactly `lateralDelay` with values like `0.22` through `0.31` with no added modifier. I had a strong hunch NNLC and/or model is negatively affected by the total delay being too low. It's never been tested this low before. Now some preliminary testing with increasing **Adjust Sofware Delay** seems to have improved model behavior for me. Other people need to test this.
I have not looked at the NNLC-disabled codepath at all. Somebody needs to test that too on a car where no-NNLC works well like Kia EV6+VFoFv3.
Increasing delay is one of the things Torqboi recommended trying while debugging a model (to try to cope with bad controls).
Keep in mind for whoever reads this, this adjusted delay is with liveDelay not being used in the current path
The NNLC learned lag merge reduced `lateralDelay` without modifier whenever NNLC is enabled. That's in `master-new` as of June 24th.
You're talking about two different things btw
Sort of. That was a huge unexpected reduction for people with NNLC enabled. PR #1001 lets you override that by turning off the Learner toggle and choosing a value.
I'm saying PR #946 made model behavior slightly worse. My theory is dropping it all the way to `lateralDelay` was too much. PR #1001 lets users attempt to figure out where is the sweet spot.
If you have an issue with the first pr, take it up with the author Dr. twilsonco

`LATERAL_LAG_MOD = 0.0 # seconds, modifies how far in the future we look ahead for the lateral plan`
Nothing was wrong with his PR. We added s/0.3/0.1/ after testing it, then that was changed to 0.0 seconds immediately before merge.
Yes. Per twilsonco
OK, if he asked for it, I think he was wrong.
Okay.
Tell him then
Not a big deal. We have the tools to figure out a sweet spot now.
I sent twilsonco a summary
@discountchubbs btw what is your typical learned `lateralDelay`?
.20 for total

In comparison to TR14:

This model seems to be be slightly more centered in the lane however it feels hesitant and makes larger steering inputs when trying to take turns on city streets. It feels like it hesitates when performing a lane change like it doesn’t want to commit fully to the change for a fraction of a second before it goes. 

It also feels more jerky both on the highway and in the city when making turns and adjusting to stay in the center of the lane. It seems to wait and then put in a larger steering inputs.

Overall for me it seems like a side step from TR14. I can see where depending on the steering torque of a car this model would work better but for my car it’s a step in the wrong direction.
